purpose: Keep every Black-Ink page easy and satisfying to color: the monster is the large centered focal subject, while an accurate varied environment frames and supports the story.
benchmark_notes: Comparable bold-and-easy coloring books emphasize large, bold, simple designs and easy-to-color spaces.
Black-Ink keeps that accessibility but uses richer fantasy environments and stronger creature identity.

primary_subject.placement: centered or near-centered in the primary visual field
primary_subject.rule: The monster is the largest and first-read object on the page, centered or near-centered, normally occupying about 60–75% of page height. Keep the full or nearly full silhouette readable while leaving a surrounding environmental frame.

environment.rule: Use two to four large environment-defining forms arranged around and behind the monster. The habitat must read clearly but remain visually secondary.

story_prop.rule: Story-critical props must be large enough to recognize and color comfortably, but remain visually subordinate to the monster unless the story explicitly depends on scale contrast.

negative_space.rule: Preserve broad white regions between major shapes so marker and pencil users can color without fighting line density.

shape_rules: The monster is the dominant central focal shape and should be the first thing the eye reads.
Keep the full or nearly full monster silhouette visible; avoid cropping major anatomy unless the page concept explicitly requires a close-up.
Favor broad contiguous coloring regions over tiny enclosed islands.
Use bold outer contours and lighter simpler interior detail.
Build the environment from a few large colorable forms such as arches, rocks, trees, ruins, doors, stairs, pillars, shelves, or ledges.
Avoid micro-texture such as repeated scales, fur strokes, cracks, pebbles, bubbles, leaves, barnacles, bricks, coins, or rubble unless only a few are needed for identity.
Frame the monster with environment forms instead of placing equally dominant objects beside it.
Story-critical props must remain readable but visually subordinate to the monster.
Background depth should come from overlap and perspective of large forms, not from filling empty space with tiny objects.
Do not add a decorative rectangular artwork frame or inset page border; use clean white page margins only.
Secondary creatures may support a story beat, but they must remain smaller, simpler, and visually subordinate to the primary monster.
Represent repeated materials such as coins, chainmail, scales, masonry, fur, webs, and rubble with selective marks and larger grouped regions rather than exhaustive tiny repetition.
Every creature must have readable physical grounding: visible contact with a support surface, or explicit and believable airborne/hanging motion logic.
A creature in midair may not use a neutral standing pose; center of gravity, limb gesture, and source/trajectory cues must explain why it is airborne.

environment_object_scale.major_objects: large enough to color comfortably and recognize at thumbnail size
environment_object_scale.tiny_objects: avoid unless essential to the story or identity

automatic_failures: monster is small, off-center without narrative purpose, or visually secondary to the environment
monster fills nearly the entire page and erases habitat identity
environment consists mostly of tiny repeated details
too many small enclosed coloring cells
story-critical object is too small to recognize
large foreground object blocks monster anatomy without narrative purpose
background is empty because detail reduction removed all habitat cues
decorative rectangular artwork border or inset page frame
secondary figures compete with the primary monster for attention
repeated micro-patterns turn large colorable surfaces into many tiny cells
creature appears to hover because feet or body do not contact any support and no airborne action is readable
falling or jumping creature uses a static standing pose in midair

reference_composition.placement: centered or near-centered; full or nearly full silhouette visible
reference_composition.environment_role: frame the monster around and behind it using large readable shapes
reference_composition.prop_rule: story props readable but visually subordinate to the monster
reference_composition.line_rule: strong outer contour, simpler interior detail, broad white coloring regions
